interest: War Minister Sadao Araki secretly sold Peru new 75 mm guns during the Leticia Conflict, 1932–33.
overview: State Department decimal file 894.20123 (September 1932 to May 1934) documents United States diplomatic and naval surveillance of a Peruvian military mission dispatched to Japan under Lieutenant Colonel Felipe de la Barra, accompanied by Captains Enrique Indacochea and Juan Mendoza Rodríguez, during the Leticia dispute with Colombia. Initially presented as a mission to observe Japanese Army maneuvers, the mission sought to procure modern field artillery, machine guns, aircraft, and munitions from the Japanese War Office, attempting to arrange barter transactions exchanging Peruvian guano or petroleum through the Okura Trading Company. Although barter proposals collapsed due to resistance from Japan's synthetic fertilizer cartel and American corporate dominance of Peruvian oil, Captain Indacochea remained covertly in Tokyo and, with the intervention of Japanese War Minister General Sadao Araki, secured a secret agreement to purchase several batteries of newly developed 75 mm field guns, 37 mm infantry guns, and grenades for cash, taking advantage of the devalued yen. U.S. diplomats in Lima, Tokyo, and Bogotá closely tracked these transactions and subsequent reciprocal visits, highlighting growing Japanese commercial-military overtures in Latin America.

subfiles.about: Reporting the departure from Callao of a Peruvian military commission to Japan aboard the Japanese steamer Bokuyo Maru.
subfiles.from: William C. Burdett (First Secretary of Embassy, Lima)
subfiles.summary: Lima reports a three-officer Peruvian military commission leaving for Japan on the Bokuyo Maru, September 1932, arranged with the Japanese Legation.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2133 from Lima on Peruvian Military Mission to Japan

subfiles.about: Transmitting Lima's despatch No. 2133 to Tokyo and citing reports of guano-for-arms barter negotiations.
subfiles.from: William R. Castle, Jr. (For the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: State forwards Lima's report to Grew, noting Peru's plan to trade guano revenue for Japanese arms.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 119 from Department of State to Tokyo on Peruvian Military Mission

subfiles.about: Cross-referencing Lima Telegram No. 178 regarding arrangements to exchange guano for Japanese arms.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Lima Telegram No. 178 on a Peruvian mission to Japan to trade guano for arms.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Lima Telegram No. 178 on Guano-for-Arms Barter

subfiles.about: Reporting the departure of the Peruvian arms mission to Japan amidst escalating military tensions with Colombia over Leticia.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Dearing reports a Peruvian arms mission departing for Japan amid border clashes with Colombia at Leticia.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 178 from Lima on Leticia Conflict and Arms Mission to Japan

subfiles.about: Transmitting an ONI intelligence report from the Eleventh Naval District regarding the arrival of Peruvian officers in California.
subfiles.from: Captain Hayne Ellis (Director of Naval Intelligence)
subfiles.summary: The Director of Naval Intelligence transmits to Edwin C. Wilson at the State Department's Division of Latin American Affairs an intelligence report from the Commandant of the Eleventh Naval District. The report details the transit of the Peruvian military officers through California on their way to Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Director of Naval Intelligence Transmitting Report on Peruvian Officers
subfiles.to: Edwin C. Wilson (Division of Latin American Affairs, Department of State)

subfiles.about: Reporting the arrival of Peruvian officers in San Pedro and passenger intelligence regarding munitions purchases.
subfiles.summary: Eleventh Naval District reports Peruvian officers passing through San Pedro to Japan; a fellow passenger said their real aim was buying munitions.
subfiles.title: Intelligence Report from Eleventh Naval District on Arrival of Peruvian Military Mission at San Pedro

subfiles.about: Acknowledging receipt of the Office of Naval Intelligence report regarding Peruvian military officers.
subfiles.from: Edwin C. Wilson (Division of Latin American Affairs, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Edwin C. Wilson of the Division of Latin American Affairs thanks Captain Hayne Ellis of the Office of Naval Intelligence for providing the intelligence report from the Commandant of the Eleventh Naval District.
subfiles.title: Letter from Edwin C. Wilson Acknowledging Naval Intelligence Report
subfiles.to: Captain Hayne Ellis (Director of Naval Intelligence)

subfiles.about: Cross-referencing Tokyo Despatch No. 174 concerning the arrival of Peruvian officers in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Tokyo Despatch No. 174 on three Peruvian officers' arrival, presumably to barter guano for arms.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Tokyo Despatch No. 174 on Arrival of Peruvian Officers

subfiles.about: Extract from a Tokyo political report discussing the secret Peruvian military mission and Japanese arms export efforts.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo report extract: Peruvian officers arrive secretly on an arms-for-guano mission as Japan uses the cheap yen to sell munitions.
subfiles.title: Extract from Tokyo Despatch No. 174 on Japanese-Peruvian Relations and Munitions

subfiles.about: Division memorandum advising officers to read Tokyo Despatch No. 216 in full.
subfiles.summary: A brief internal State Department memorandum from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs noting that Ambassador Grew's Despatch No. 216 of December 3, 1932, provides important details regarding the Peruvian military mission and recommends that it be read in full.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 216

subfiles.about: Comprehensive report from Ambassador Grew analyzing Peruvian weapons shopping, price inquiries, and failed barter schemes.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports the Peruvian mission surveying Japanese weapons; the Okura guano barter failed and oil barter faced obstacles, so cash purchases were likely.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 216 from Tokyo on Peruvian Military Mission and Barter Negotiations

subfiles.about: Internal handwritten assessment of Peruvian Chargé d'Affaires Carlos Bailey Lembcke in Tokyo.
subfiles.from: H. F. M. (Division of Latin American Affairs)
subfiles.summary: A brief departmental note by an officer in the Division of Latin American Affairs characterizing Carlos Bailey Lembcke, the Peruvian Chargé d'Affaires in Tokyo, as unreliable and prone to long-winded talk.
subfiles.title: Note on Peruvian Chargé d'Affaires Carlos Bailey Lembcke

subfiles.about: Division memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 222 regarding conversations with the Peruvian Chargé.
subfiles.summary: An internal State Department memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 222. It recounts the Peruvian Chargé d'Affaires' denial of guano-for-arms barter schemes, his assertion that Japanese arms are too heavy for Peru, and his anxiety regarding Colombian naval moves on the Amazon.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 222

subfiles.about: Transmitting a memorandum of conversation with Peruvian Chargé d'Affaires Lembcke concerning rumors and Colombia.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew transmits a memorandum of a conversation held between Counselor Edwin L. Neville and Peruvian Chargé d'Affaires Carlos Bailey Lembcke on December 10, 1932. Grew notes that garbled rumors regarding Foreign Office discussions reached the Chargé and observes that strained Peruvian-Colombian relations are driving statements made in South America.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 222 from Tokyo Transmitting Memorandum of Conversation with Peruvian Chargé

subfiles.about: Detailed record of interview with Peruvian Chargé Lembcke denying barter and expressing fear of Colombian aggression.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville (Counselor of Embassy, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Peruvian Chargé Carlos Bailey Lembcke tells Neville guano-for-arms barter is fantastic and voices alarm at Colombian Amazon preparations.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation with Peruvian Chargé d'Affaires Carlos Bailey Lembcke

subfiles.about: Cross-referencing Instruction No. 148 to Tokyo regarding Japanese proposals for a Peruvian mixed civilian-military mission.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Instruction No. 148 on Japan urging Peru to send a mission to inspect arms factories.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Department Instruction No. 148 on Proposed Peruvian Mixed Mission

subfiles.about: Division memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 241 regarding the Peruvian Military Mission.
subfiles.summary: A short memorandum by the Division of Far Eastern Affairs stating that Tokyo's Despatch No. 241 of December 29, 1932, indicates no new developments have occurred concerning the Peruvian Military Mission in Japan.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 241

subfiles.about: Reporting that no new developments have occurred regarding the Peruvian Military Mission in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew acknowledges receipt of Department Instruction No. 148 of December 5, 1932. He states that no subsequent developments have altered the situation described in his previous despatches (Nos. 216 and 222) and promises continued vigilance.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 241 from Tokyo Reporting No New Developments Regarding Peruvian Mission

subfiles.about: Transmitting memoranda of conversations with Electric Boat Company officials concerning Peruvian naval vessels.
subfiles.from: William R. Castle, Jr. (For the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: The State Department sends Ambassador Grew in Tokyo copies of two memoranda of conversation held in March and November 1932 with an official of the Electric Boat Company of New York. The discussions concerned vessels constructed by the American firm for the Peruvian Government.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 187 from Department of State to Tokyo Transmitting Electric Boat Company Memoranda

subfiles.about: Cross-referencing Instruction No. 127 regarding Japanese efforts to monopolize Peruvian arms purchases in exchange for oil.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Instruction No. 127: Japan offered to buy Peru's petroleum if Peru bought all its arms in Japan.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Department Instruction No. 127 on Japanese Munitions and Petroleum Barter Offers

subfiles.about: Division memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 499 regarding secret artillery purchases and Araki's Peruvian decoration.
subfiles.summary: FE memo on Tokyo Despatch No. 499: Captain Indacochea secretly agreed for Japan to supply 75 mm and 37 mm guns and grenades to Peru.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 499

subfiles.about: Routing note calling attention to Tokyo's report on clandestine arms sales to Peru.
subfiles.from: H. F. M. (Division of Latin American Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Routing slip calling Tokyo's report on Japanese arms sales to Peru of extreme interest.
subfiles.title: Division of Latin American Affairs Routing Slip on Tokyo Despatch No. 499
subfiles.to: Edwin C. Wilson (Division of Latin American Affairs)

subfiles.about: Reporting a secret agreement orchestrated by General Araki for Japan to sell modern 75 mm field guns and munitions to Peru.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville (Counselor of Embassy, Tokyo, for the Ambassador)
subfiles.summary: Neville reports Araki pushed through a secret sale of Japan's newest 75 mm field guns to Peru, concealed from the United States.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 499 from Tokyo on Secret Peruvian Contract for Japanese 75 mm Artillery

subfiles.about: Cross-referencing Bogotá Despatch No. 5854 discussing the reported Japanese-Peruvian arms agreement.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Bogotá Despatch No. 5854 on a reported Japan–Peru arms agreement.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Bogotá Despatch No. 5854 on Japanese-Peruvian Arms Agreement

subfiles.about: Transmitting Bogotá Despatch No. 5854 concerning Japanese arms sales to Peru to the American Ambassador in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits to Ambassador Grew in Tokyo a copy of Despatch No. 5854 from the American Legation in Bogotá, Colombia, regarding the reported agreement between Japan and Peru for arms and ammunition. Grew is instructed to keep the enclosed intelligence strictly confidential.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 376 from Department of State to Tokyo Transmitting Bogotá Despatch No. 5854

subfiles.about: Cross-referencing Lima Despatch No. 3425 concerning the reciprocal visit of a Japanese military mission to Peru.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Lima Despatch No. 3425 on a Japanese Military Mission's visit to Peru, May 1934.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Lima Despatch No. 3425 on Japanese Military Mission to Peru
